runs.name: Usinas Siderurgicas de Minas Gerais S.A., Usiminas; Brazil, not an SEC registrant (EDGAR holds only the BNY Mellon F-6 facilities, the last 2017), OTC ADR one to one, B3 USIM3, USIM5 and USIM6; Ternium/Tenaris control, the NSC Group's stake sold to Ternium and approved by CADE in January 2026, the T/T group then at 71.02% of the common; no rename or split; its documents name no rival, CSN, Gerdau and ArcelorMittal taken as Brazilian 20-F filers
runs.box: OUT AT Q2; integrity facts recorded, not judged
runs.entry: Price **R$ 7.15** per class A preferred (USIM5, B3, 2026-10-13; Yahoo chart, aggregator, flagged, the day's volume read zero so possibly the last trade, 2026-10-09 close R$ 7.30; the ADR USNZY **US$ 1.40**, thin). The ADR's class inferred by the analyst from price parity over 429 days (median 1.028 against USIM5, 1.052 against USIM3), the F-6 filings naming no ticker. Shares **1,230,942,660** outstanding (702,734,028 ON and 528,208,632 PN, issued less treasury, CVM capital composition, ITR 2026-06-30, CVM document 159792); cap **R$ 8,801M**; net cash **R$ 499M** at 2026-06-30 on the company's figure, forfaiting R$ 570.1M at 2025-12-31 beside. Sovereign **12.57%** (Tesouro Nacional, NTN-F 2037-01-01, purchase rate 2026-10-09). Filings read, all from the CVM: DFP FY2025 (154757, 2026-02-13), FY2023 v2, FY2021, FY2019, FY2017; ITR 2026-06-30 with the 2Q26 release; Formulario de Referencia 2026 v7 (159805); CVM open data 2016 to 2026; the English 2025 annual report. One figure cross-checked (FY2025 revenue R$ 26,263,450 thousand, structured statement, segment note 30 and Formulario 1.3). `tools/run.py` and `cover_shares.py` returned not an SEC filer; all arithmetic by hand. Lines of evidence derived by the analyst from the Formulario sections 1, 2, 4, 8 and 11 and the DFP notes (the brief's departure), stated in the run file. Competitors: the company names none ("demais usinas"); CSN steel segment, Gerdau Brazil and ArcelorMittal Brazil read from their 20-Fs as a choice of the analyst, ArcelorMittal Brasil itself and the importers flagged as not SEC filers. Owner cash after interest, the company's own tax and minority dividends, 2016 to 2025, R$ M: (551), 642, 37, 1,230, 2,910, 3,569, (1,414), 1,263, (99), 925; ten-year average 851, all-equity 1,046; spending R$ 11,078M against depreciation R$ 10,859M over the decade. Balance sheets 2016 to 2026-06 read in Step 0: no goodwill; debt R$ 5.1bn to 6.9bn throughout while cash tripled, net debt about R$ 4.7bn (2016) to net cash; equity up R$ 7.5bn in 2021, R$ 3.0bn given back since the 2024 peak; the 2025 loss of R$ 2.9bn carrying a R$ 2,214M steel impairment and a R$ 1,284M deferred tax charge. Q1 IN (two segments, the economics readable off the figures; Brazil's governance a reason to ask a lower price, not a pass). **Q2 OUT**: steel decides at 59.5% of 2021 to 2025 segment operating profit (66.7% as reported), a share resting on 2021 alone (over 2022 to 2025 steel R$ (453)M, mining R$ 2,106M), written down by the analyst; steel operating margin the lowest of the four mills in six of ten years 2016 to 2025, below Gerdau Brazil in all ten and ArcelorMittal Brazil in nine, 5.4% over the decade (0.9% without 2021) against CSN 8.4%, Gerdau Brazil 13.4%, ArcelorMittal Brazil 14.3%; the domestic price held near "subsidized import prices" in the filer's words, imports 25.6% of consumption in 2025 and more than three times 2020, revenue per tonne down 4% in 2025; Cubatao's primary steelmaking stopped 2015, its blast furnaces written off 2021, slabs bought from the controller's Ternium Brasil under a R$ 4,344M contract; the field's integrated flat-steel mills below ordinary returns over the cycle; contrary evidence recorded (H1 2026 steel margin 7.5% after the 2026 trade measures, credited only after a full cycle). Q3 to Q12 not reached. **Integrity facts recorded, not judged:** the controlling group also slab supplier, engineering contractor (Techint), raw-materials buyer (Exiros) and customer (SIAT, Confab), royalties to Nippon Steel; control changed in January 2026 at about US$ 2.06 a common share; Adjusted EBITDA headlined beside a net loss, a next-quarter outlook given; officers' pay R$ 29.3M in 2025. After the stop: no buyback, no acquisition in ten years, a R$ 1,050M capital increase in 2016, blast-furnace and coke-plant rebuilds announced to 2029. COMPUTATION beneath the stop: cycle base 2016 to 2025 (specific (a), 2021 the decade's peak), all-spending case central (specific (e)), decline between cycle halves carried as the bottom; all-equity interest shield at 34% (a CONVENTION of the run); value range **R$ 5.51 to R$ 7.17** a share all-equity against R$ 7.15, equity-only R$ 5.46 to 5.50; the no-growth case earns the floor at the price (12.60% on EV), the declining case does not; fair price **R$ 7.78 all-equity**, **R$ 6.89 equity-only**; not armed, the box being OUT at Q2. Contamination declared by the analyst: one filtered `Test Runs/` file-name listing for the company's names that returned nothing; the SID run's commit subjects in its opening context (CSN figures taken from CSN's own 20-Fs, the sovereign fetched independently). Commits 9d9558f8 to 8ccee366, four; a 294 KB extract (`data/usim_DMPL_con.csv`) committed in 5b79a86f and removed in the next commit, so it stays in history. Position note filled at the fold: not held (`PORTFOLIO.md` carries no line for USNZY, USDMY, USIM3, USIM5, USIM6, Usiminas or Usinas Siderurgicas). Citations: the analyst's `check_cites.py` clean (33 ids, 17 fragments); the dispatcher's `_dispatcher_cite_check.py` 33 ids, 14 quoted cites, no missing id, no E-id, no slip. No tracked research file over 200 KB. check_framework PASS. **For the operator:** the analyst's gaps: (1) the floor of about ten percent below the BRL sovereign of 12.57%, so the all-equity fair price (R$ 7.78) sits above the top of the range (as in GGB and SID); (2) Q2's business-of-parts threshold has no cycle rule, and one peak year chose the deciding part; (3) whether parts are measured before or after equity-method income; (4) a company that names no rival leaves the choice to the analyst; (5) the ADR's class not stated in any filing; (6) zero nominal growth after year ten against a nominal BRL rate. Could not get: cost per tonne (margins stand in), like-shaped rival segments, the sum of possible-loss contingencies.
runs.narr: Q2 OUT: steel decides (59.5% of 2021 to 2025 segment operating profit, resting on 2021 alone), not the low-cost producer: lowest steel margin of four Brazilian mills in six of ten years 2016 to 2025, below Gerdau Brazil in all ten and ArcelorMittal Brazil in nine, 5.4% over the decade against 8.4% to 14.3%; price held near subsidized import prices in the filer's words, imports tripled since 2020; Cubatao's steelmaking closed, slabs bought from the controller. Integrity facts recorded, not judged: Ternium/Tenaris control and related-party contracts, the January 2026 control sale, Adjusted EBITDA headlined beside a loss. COMPUTATION beneath the stop: all-equity range R$ 5.51 to 7.17 against R$ 7.15 (USIM5, the ADR one to one), net cash R$ 499M, fair R$ 7.78 all-equity, R$ 6.89 equity-only, not armed. Framework gaps for the operator: the BRL sovereign above the floor; no cycle rule in the parts threshold; rivals the company does not name.
